findings.evidence: mathlib_cache.py:60-65 `release_cache_published(gh, repo, sha, tag, known_on_master=None)` ... `if (known_on_master or (lambda: on_master(gh, repo, sha)))()`; mathlib_cache.py:57 `gh(f"repos/{repo}/compare/{sha}...{BRANCH}")`; resolve_deps.py:164-167 passes `on_master` for exactly this reason; check-bump.sh:165 already fetched `compare/$REV_P...$BRANCH`.
findings.fix: Pass the known answer through, as resolve_deps.py:160-167 already does: hand `on_branch` (when `$BRANCH` = master) into the heredoc and call `release_cache_published(gh_api, slug, rev, tag, known_on_master=lambda: known)`; if the two-way log message were dropped, `cache_published(gh_api, slug, rev, tag, known_on_master)` replaces the whole composition.
findings.issue: The embedded python re-derives `mathlib_cache.cache_published` (`master_build_published(...) or (tag and release_cache_published(...))`, mathlib_cache.py:69-72) and calls `release_cache_published` without `known_on_master`, so it issues `compare/$REV_P...master` a second time — the shell already made that exact call at line 165 and stored the answer in `on_branch` (line 167-168).

findings.evidence: lean_versions.py:54-64 `why_not_newer`; check-bump.sh:104,178 call it via `lean_versions.py newer`; resolve_deps.py:298-306 duplicates parse/backward/equal by hand (line 305 reduces to `why_not_newer(self.toolchain, self.mathlib_toolchain(m)) is not None` once lines 298 and 300 have passed).
findings.fix: Import `why_not_newer` in resolve_deps.py and replace line 305 with `if why_not_newer(self.toolchain, self.mathlib_toolchain(m)): return None`.
findings.issue: `forward` keeps its own 'strictly newer toolchain' test (`parse_toolchain(mathlib_toolchain(m)) <= parse_toolchain(self.toolchain)`) while the guard now asks the same question through the new `lean_versions.why_not_newer`. lean_versions.py:3-5 states the rule lives there once precisely so the resolver cannot propose a move the guard rejects; leaving a parallel copy reinstates the drift it guards against.

summary: The fake-gh extraction and the lean_versions CLI are real de-duplications, but step 2b re-implements mathlib_cache.cache_published and re-queries master membership the shell already holds, and resolve_deps.forward keeps a hand-rolled copy of the new why_not_newer rule the module exists to hold once.
